patch_description: Uses a sparse set of two-hop interactions, retaining only the strongest relay candidates for each positive-demand OD pair. Relay affinity depends on both legs: the weaker leg limits the score, while the stronger leg provides a small supporting signal. This reduces rewards for paths that look attractive only because of one leg. Direct-link rewards remain demand-based, with a modest concave component so medium-sized demands still influence the topology. Pressure discounts relays at nodes with high incident demand. The sparse path terms also keep the interaction graph smaller than the dense two-hop construction.
